raw_response:
Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate a massive right-sided pneumothorax with significant mediastinal shift to the right and an abnormal, displaced cardiac silhouette, which are classic radiographic signs of right-sided cardiac herniation through a pericardial defect following pneumonectomy. This mechanical strangulation and displacement explain the acute haemodynamic compromise on post-operative day 1.
